message: In the under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit, the vertical comfort at about 1.9 Hertz (Hz) has needed independent check against crowd walking limits, Structural Dynamics Lead. To check it I used standards review reusing the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6) against the resonant response calculation (E1). I found about 0.20 metres per second squared controlled versus 1.75 metres per second squared lively baseline, below the 0.5 metres per second squared maximum comfort limit, according to Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), 2008. I propose accepting Comfort Class 1 (CL1) meaning maximum comfort as the build target with effective damping above 3 percent. In the concealed support frame, the under-deck install and re-tuning access has risk of deck closure and drift off tune, Retrofit Integration Architect and Vibration Control Specialist. To check it I used build review reusing the concealed mounting cross-section (E7) with the optimal TMD sizing (E4). I found two 200 kilogram units fit below the soffit with 30 millimetre clearance for 8.2 millimetre stroke with no deck penetration, according to Sétra, 2006. I propose night works from below in halves with bolted cross-frames, lockable hatches, corrosion-protected springs and dampers, and shim re-tuning for 5 to 10 percent frequency variation. My position: not ready because connection fatigue and tuning robustness need joint review.
